comment: What each Linux build adds on top of the upstream release it is made from.
The key is the full tag without its release- prefix, as in 3.6.6-linux1.
generate-release-notes.ts turns the entries into a section of the release
notes, above the upstream changelog. Leaving a version out of this file is
fine: the section is then left out too.
This file is ours. It sits next to the upstream changelog.json rather than
inside it, so that merging an upstream release never conflicts here.

3.6.11-beta1-linux2: Preview build, made from the upstream 3.6.11 beta 1: it carries what the next release will bring, and the bugs a beta comes with

Security update, recommended: the bundled Git moves to 2.56.1, which fixes six vulnerabilities. The most serious lets a malicious repository run code on the machine when it is cloned along with its submodules, which is how GitHub Desktop clones. GitHub Desktop uses its own Git, so updating the Git of the system does not cover it: <https://github.blog/open-source/git/git-security-vulnerabilities-announced-7/>

"Show in your File Manager" asks the file manager already running to show the folder, instead of starting it again: Dolphin opens it in a new tab when set to, rather than in a new window holding the tabs of its last session
Otherwise the same application as 3.6.11-beta1-linux1, whose notes list what the upstream beta brings, several accounts at once among them
The bundled git keeps its commands as links, as in earlier builds: the upstream beta copies them in full instead, which doubles the size of the installed app
Also available as a Flatpak, from the beta channel of the package repository or as a .flatpak file: either way, flatpak update brings the betas that follow
The package repository serves the .deb, the .rpm and the Flatpak on its beta channel, and keeps them up to date through apt, dnf, zypper or flatpak: <https://packages-github-desktop.nitramo.fr/>
Beta channel features are enabled, as in the official beta builds
The window shows its own icon under Wayland, and groups with its launcher in the taskbar
Ptyxis is detected as a terminal, along with the editors and shells upstream added since 3.4.13

3.6.11-beta1-linux1: Preview build, made from the upstream 3.6.11 beta 1: it carries what the next release will bring, and the bugs a beta comes with

Several accounts at once, new in this beta, change how credentials are stored and handed to git: on Linux they go through the Secret Service (KWallet or GNOME Keyring), so problems signing in, switching accounts or pushing over HTTPS are the most useful to report
The bundled git keeps its commands as links, as in earlier builds: the upstream beta copies them in full instead, which doubles the size of the installed app
Also available as a Flatpak, from the beta channel of the package repository or as a .flatpak file: either way, flatpak update brings the betas that follow
The package repository serves the .deb, the .rpm and the Flatpak on its beta channel, and keeps them up to date through apt, dnf or flatpak: <https://packages-github-desktop.nitramo.fr/>
The .deb and .rpm packages are numbered below the 3.6.11 release they precede, so that apt and dnf move on to that release once it is out
Beta channel features are enabled, as in the official beta builds
The window shows its own icon under Wayland, and groups with its launcher in the taskbar
Ptyxis is detected as a terminal, along with the editors and shells upstream added since 3.4.13
3.6.10-linux1: Follows 3.6.7-linux1: no Linux build was made from upstream 3.6.8 and 3.6.9, so this one also brings their changes, listed only in their own release notes: <https://github.com/desktop/desktop/releases/tag/release-3.6.8> and <https://github.com/desktop/desktop/releases/tag/release-3.6.9>. Among them: short-lived tokens for new sign-ins, Git 2.56.0, Electron 44.9.1, SSH host key prompts that work with newer OpenSSH, and no more crash when Copilot stops unexpectedly
